name_in_paper: experimental challenge with mosquito-borne falciparum malaria

evidence.quote: Thirty-nine vaccine recipients were assessed at study entry; on the day of the third vaccination; at 24 h, 72 h, and 2 weeks after vaccination; and on day 5 after challenge.
Infection with malaria was determined by detection of parasite in malaria thick blood smears during the 30 days after challenge.

Preparation of cellular RNA and subsequent processing for GeneChip analysis were performed as described elsewhere [28], by use of the HG-U133 A 2.0 and HG-U133 Plus 2.0 GeneChips (Affymetrix) and the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer system (Agilent Technologies), to assess the integrity and quantity of RNA.
Prediction analysis of microarrays identified genes corresponding with protection.
Gene set enrichment analysis identified sets of genes associated with protection after the third vaccination and before challenge.

Differentially expressed genes were identified using the statistical program Significance Analysis of Microarrays (SAM; version 3.0) [31], and cluster analysis of microarray data sets was performed using the MultiExperiment Viewer.

Principal component analysis, which is an eigen vector–based multivariate tool that reveals the most informative trends in complex data sets by identifying the predominant gradients in data sets, was performed using Partek Pro (version 6.0; Partek).

To confirm observations from the gene chip data, TaqMan Gene Expression Assays (Applied Biosystems) were used to detect genes in the immunoproteosome pathway (PSME2, PSMB9, PSMB6, and PSMA4) in 3 randomly chosen samples from protected and nonprotected persons, at 2 weeks after the third vaccination.

Preparation of cellular RNA and subsequent processing for GeneChip analysis were performed as described elsewhere [28], by use of the HG-U133 A 2.0 and HG-U133 Plus 2.0 GeneChips (Affymetrix) and the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer system (Agilent Technologies), to assess the integrity and quantity of RNA.
